subject.name_or_desc: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, Lord General of the Parliament's army

context.question: Event figure: what success, honour and issue should the Earl have from this his last expedition into the West?
context.asked_at: The time of his Excellency the Earl of Essex his last setting forth into the West, 1644 (event moment; the day is not stated in the text).
context.setting: An event figure (not a posed question): the scheme of the time of the Earl's last setting forth into the West in 1644, judged by Lilly for posterity.

attachments.key_positions: Saturn, Venus and Mercury having dignities in the Ascendant; the Moon separating from a trine of Saturn and applying to a square of Mars, lord of his (the Earl's) second and ninth houses (substance, assistants, friends, journeys); the Dragon's Tail in the Ascendant; Saturn, lord of the Ascendant, peregrine and in his fall in the second; the Moon in her detriment; the Part of Fortune disposed by Mercury, lord of the seventh, a significator of his enemies
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II: the time of his Excellency the Earl of Essex his last setting forth into the West (printed p.473; Fig. 31 in the 1852 Zadkiel edition)
